pages.raw_meta: Covista is America's largest healthcare educator, expanding access to healthcare careers and delivering workforce solutions at scale. Discover the Covista story.
raw_blocks: America faces a workforce shortage across the sectors that matter most: healthcare, veterinary medicine, education and business. We don't have enough professionals to meet growing demands. Organizations are investing in technology and innovation, but technology alone won't solve this crisis. Meaningful progress requires people—and higher education models built for how they actually live and work.
The future lies in education built for working adults who bring the maturity and real-world experience healthcare needs. The challenge is building these pathways at scale.
We exist to solve this challenge.

Every year, our five accredited institutions graduate 26,000 healthcare professionals—more than any other educator in America. We're unlocking exceptional talent at scale through a fundamentally different model—one that both expands access and prepares practice-ready graduates.
Expanding access to healthcare careers

We make quality education accessible to working adults, career changers and non-traditional students that conventional education misses, unlocking talent the healthcare system needs but hasn't been able to access.

Our graduates enter the workforce ready from day one—clinically skilled, hands-on prepared and comfortable with AI-powered tools. For employers, this means professionals who can hit the ground running.
We partner directly with hospitals and healthcare providers to build programs that lead to employment after graduation.
Serving communities that need care most

We place our graduates in underserved rural and urban communities, improving patient outcomes by increasing the number of healthcare providers who can work closer to home, among the people that know them best.

We foster a purpose-driven culture that empowers our 10,000 faculty and colleagues to develop new skills, build meaningful careers that match their ambitions and have a tangible impact on health education and workforce development.
"The workforce shortage is intensifying. We're removing barriers to education and expanding pathways at scale—so more people can join the solution."
Steve Beard Chairman and CEO
Covista (pronounced co-vis-tah) blends two powerful ideas: "co" standing for community, collaboration and partnership and "vista" referencing future and vision.
Together, Covista communicates a shared vision of the future.
Explore the principles that ground our existence, guide our actions and bring our company to life.
The executive team and Board of Directors expanding access to healthcare careers and delivering workforce solutions at scale.
We’re embedding AI into clinical education across all five institutions, preparing graduates to apply AI tools in practice from day one.

Covista is America's largest healthcare educator, serving 100,000 students through five accredited institutions: American University of the Caribbean School of Medicine, Chamberlain University, Ross University School of Medicine, Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine and Walden University. Through personalized, tech-enabled education powered by 10,000 faculty and colleagues, we expand access to healthcare careers and address the U.S. healthcare workforce shortage at scale.

Our purpose is to open doors and unlock potential—developing skilled, compassionate professionals who strengthen healthcare and improve patient outcomes in their communities. 26,000 healthcare professionals graduate annually from our programs joining a community of more than 400,000 alumni—300,000 of whom are healthcare professionals who deliver care across the country.

Our outcomes demonstrate this commitment: a 97% first-time residency attainment rate* at our medical schools, #1 and #3 rankings for our nursing schools (Chamberlain and Walden) and the #1 provider of DVM graduates (Ross Veterinary). Through partnerships with hospitals and healthcare providers, we’re connecting education directly to employment pathways and building sustainable workforce pipelines that support America’s healthcare needs.

We reach students that traditional programs miss—working adults, career changers, and non-traditional students who thought healthcare careers were closed to them. We design education around students' lives—offering flexible pathways that make healthcare careers accessible to people who thought that door was closed. Our graduates are practice ready from day one. Through partnering with leaders such as Google Cloud and, Hippocratic AI, we work to integrate AI and technology directly into clinical education. Students develop skills in our simulation labs and complete clinical rotations at hundreds of partner hospitals and healthcare systems—learning the workflows, technology and protocols they'll use in practice. This is how we deliver workforce solutions at scale.

*Percent of students attaining a 2026-27 residency position out of all graduates or expected graduates in 2025-26 who were active applicants in the 2026 NRMP match or who attained a residency position outside the NRMP match

pages.raw_meta: Covista healthcare partnerships strengthen workforce pipelines, preparing practice-ready graduates and upskilled staff for quality patient care.
raw_blocks: Every health provider faces different workforce challenges. We design solutions tailored to your system’s specific needs—nursing pipelines, physician pathways, behavioral health programs and more.

Students learn in your facilities and are taught according to your practices, your technology and your culture of care. By graduation, these clinicians have already been seamlessly integrated into your workforce.
Build customized, practice-ready pipelines—nurses, physicians, behavioral health specialists—learning in your facilities, your way.
Onboarding that drives faster readiness
Drive faster readiness by pulling onboarding into the course of study—so when graduates start, they already meet your standards for practice-ready.

Increase retention by preparing clinicians for your practice environments and standards of care. Structure benefits like loan repayment tied to employment commitments and create advancement pathways that give employees reasons to stay and grow within your system.
Advance unlicensed staff to BSNs, nurses to NPs, licensed staff to leadership roles. Access certificate and CME programs designed around your organization's needs and your employees' ambitions.
Our five accredited institutions deliver 26,000 healthcare graduates each year—building the sustainable talent pipelines your system needs.

SSM Health faced workforce challenges common to health systems nationwide: nursing shortages across their markets, experienced nurses nearing retirement and costly reliance on contract labor. They needed a sustainable, long-term solution to strengthen their workforce and ensure consistent care across all four states they serve.

A multi-state BSN program where students learn in SSM Health facilities, taught by a blend of Chamberlain and SSM Health faculty, using SSM Health standards. Students commit to employment in exchange for loan repayment over four years.

Programs like this drive down workforce costs by addressing turnover, reliance on travel nurses and recruiting expenses—while ensuring consistent, high-quality care. Graduates arrive on day one with institutional knowledge and a clear understanding of SSM Health’s standards of care. This program is designed to deliver:
1,200 students enrolled at full program scale
400 SSM Health-ready nurses graduating annually
4 states with sustainable talent pipelines

Advocate Health, the nation's third-largest nonprofit health system, operates across eight states with 69 hospitals and more than 1,000 care locations. Caring for communities at that scale requires a significant nursing workforce—practice-ready, specialty-trained and committed to the populations they serve. Advocate Health recognized that building that workforce requires more than traditional models of recruitment. Their People Forward, Practice Ready strategy is a long-term commitment to attracting, preparing and retaining nursing teammates, including nontraditional and working adults who have the calling—but need a different path to get there. Executing that vision required a collaborator with the capabilities, footprint and scale to match a system of their size.

A four-part program that takes a student from aspiration to practice-ready employment within Advocate Health: BSN scholarships, clinical immersion inside Advocate Health care settings, direct employment pathways and loan repayment support during employment. The collaboration is built specifically around Acute and Progressive Care—one of the most difficult and consequential roles for any health system to fill—delivered through Chamberlain's Practice Ready. Specialty Focused.® track and tailored to Advocate Health's clinical environment and patient population.

Nurses who graduate are already familiar with Advocate Health's care settings, clinical standards and patient population—reducing onboarding time and accelerating time to contribution. Recruited, trained and supported from the start of their employment, these are clinicians committed to building long-term careers at Advocate Health in the roles that matter most. The program is purpose-built to scale alongside Advocate Health's needs, expanding access to care across the communities they serve.

"Through the Aspiring Nurses program, we're not just convincing somebody who was already applying to nursing school to go from one nursing school to another, which is historically what's happened. We're actually creating access to a population across the U.S. who may believe that they haven't had the ability to pursue a career in nursing."
Amy Wilson CNO, SSM Health

"Our People Forward, Practice Ready strategy is about better attracting, preparing and retaining our nursing teammates. Chamberlain has the resources and footprint to match a system as large as ours, and their focus on nontraditional, working adults means we can reach students who might otherwise never have entered the nursing profession."
Betty Jo Rocchio EVP and CNE, Advocate Health

"The partnership with Chamberlain allows us to grow our nurses from within the community, and they are more likely to stay because this is where they got their education. As we align them with SSM Health, they get to become part of the culture and, in turn, serve the communities in which they were raised."
Dr. Marcia Lysaght SSM Regional CNO

"At Advocate Health, we believe building the healthcare workforce of tomorrow starts with removing barriers today. This collaboration with Covista creates a clear pathway for aspiring nurses—from education to employment—with the financial support they need to succeed. It reflects our commitment to growing talent from the ground up by welcoming them into an organization that will invest in their careers from the very start."
Nakesha Lopez Chief People & Culture Officer, Advocate Health

Every health system has different challenges. We design partnerships based on the healthcare staffing solutions that you need. Let's talk about what a custom workforce solution could look like for your organization.

Covista recruits and enrolls qualified candidates into a dedicated cohort for your health system. Your team gets to know applicants, and students complete clinical rotations in your facilities—taught by our faculty and yours, following your protocols. Throughout the program, students engage with your leadership through customized experiences that build institutional belonging before graduation. They’re ready to contribute from day one because they’ve already learned your workflows, technology systems and culture.

Traditional recruitment brings candidates who have been educated at any number of schools and systems. These recruits need to learn your organization and may need to “unlearn” what they have learned elsewhere. Covista partnerships deliver graduates who understand your workflows, technology, culture and standards because they developed their skills exclusively in your facilities with your workforce. This drives down the costs of turnover—travel nurses, repeated onboarding and care gaps—while ensuring continuity and consistency in patient care. You're building a sustainable workforce pipeline, not just filling open positions.

Covista is America's largest healthcare educator, graduating 26,000 healthcare professionals annually across our five accredited institutions. We partner directly with 270+ hospitals and healthcare systems across the country. We expand access to talent pools others can't reach—working adults, career changers and students in underserved communities—unlocking healthcare workforce capacity at scale. Our SSM Health partnership demonstrates what's possible at scale: 400 practice-ready nurses annually across four states, delivering consistent care quality across every facility from day one.

Yes. Covista builds custom workforce pathways designed around the specific needs of each health system we partner with—their markets, clinical environment and workforce needs. The Advocate Health collaboration is purpose-built this way: an Acute and Progressive Care specialty track tailored to their high-demand roles, delivered through Chamberlain University, the largest school of nursing in the U.S., through its Practice Ready. Specialty Focused.® model. As America's largest healthcare educator, Covista has the education infrastructure, clinical expertise and geographic reach to build this kind of custom pathway for any health system.

The model that works is built around the people in those communities rather than competing for nurses who already exist elsewhere. Covista's programs are built around the way people live—online, evenings, weekends and hybrid—reaching working adults and career changers that traditional nursing education overlooks. Rather than redistributing talent that's already too scarce, we build new nurses trained and rooted in the communities that need them most, with a direct line of sight to employment. By addressing cost, scheduling and career uncertainty, the model removes the three barriers most likely to keep qualified people out of nursing—and because Covista builds custom pathways around each system's needs, it can be scoped to a rural or critical access system's specialty gaps and geography.
